title: lava check --json
description: The one-command verification: boot, wiring, routes, features, env, commands, and the app's own suite, merged into one problem list and one exit code. `sections` says WHICH part of the app is broken before any individual problem is read; the envelope's `problems` is ordered fix-first, because a problem whose fix is a runnable command needs no judgement. It survives a failed boot on purpose — a red suite is often the reason an app cannot boot, so the tests still run and the report carries both.

sections.description: Always all eight, in the order an app is built, so a consumer can index them rather than search. A clean run has every section ok or skipped.

status.description: skipped only ever applies to `tests`. Under --strict a warn makes its section failed.

detail.description: The problem codes found, then the test summary when there was a run. Empty for a clean section.

counts.description: What boot found. All zero when the app did not boot — the counts come from the booted app, not from re-reading files.

tests.description: The suite's results, or null when no run happened — see the tests section's detail for which of --quick, --no-tests, or a missing runner it was.

strict.description: Whether warnings were escalated to failures for this run.

quick.description: Whether this run skipped the suite and the all-features sweep.
